name: Underhand Lat Pulldown with Lean Back
description: The underhand lat pulldown with an intentional lean-back combines a supinated grip (mimicking a chin-up) with a slight torso lean of 20-30 degrees, shifting the bar's target from the clavicle to the lower sternum and increasing lower lat activation. The lean also allows slightly more weight to be used than a strict upright supinated pulldown, making it effective for progressive overload on lat thickness.

execution.starting_position: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with a close to shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip. Set the thigh pad to secure the legs. Lean the torso back 20-30 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: Maintain the same lean angle throughout the set. The lean is a fixed position, not a dynamic movement.
steps: Step 1: Begin seated with arms extended, leaning back 20-30 degrees, supinated grip.
Step 2: Depress and retract the shoulder blades.
Step 3: Pull the bar to the lower chest/sternum.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at peak contraction.
Step 5: Return under control to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Leaning back too far — 20-30 degrees is sufficient; more becomes a row
Pulling to the chest instead of the sternum — the lean makes the sternum the natural target
safety_considerations: Excessive lean places stress on the lower back — keep it moderate
Ensure the thigh pad is tight to prevent pulling the body up
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to bar at lower sternum.
coaching_cues: Lean is fixed — the torso does not move during the set
Lead with the chest toward the bar
Squeeze the elbows to the sides
